messages:
Maria C.: FYI customer reported a sharp spike in signed-URL GETs from their private deployment. They see ~2k downloads across ~40 distinct IPs in the past hour. They think a signing key leaked and want urgent triage.
Samir (sec): Assigning. Which customer? paste their sample log lines and any screenshots here. We need S3 access logs + our egress gateway logs + the agent logs.
Maria C.: Customer: VelaraHealth (ticket #8891). Customer pasted: 'GET /files/patient-xyz?X-Amz-Signature=... 200 - 1.1MB 198.51.100.17' repeated many times from different IPs. Screenshot: https://files.velara/ss-8891 (customer link).
Jin Lee - oncall: On it. I'll check the private agents and the egress LB. If signed URLs were minted by our signing service, we rotate immediately. If from customer side, we coordinate containment with them.
Inga Audit: Note: audit ingestion for private tenants has ~15–20m lag atm, may not have earliest events in the dashboard. I'll pull raw S3 access logs and agent journals directly.
logbot: Starting log fetch: infra-log query --customer velarahealth --type s3_access --from 2024-11-19T12:00Z --to 2024-11-19T13:30Z --output /tmp/velara_s3_logs.json
Samir (sec): Containment checklist (proposed):
- block suspicious CIDRs at egress LB right away
- revoke short-lived tokens issued in last 2h (our side and advise customer theirs)
- rotate signing service principal and issue new key (if we find it used)
- snapshot agent and collect evidence bundle
Maria C.: Customer approved containment steps and asked us to proceed with rotation. They want log export and an incident call.
Jin Lee - oncall: Blocking top 10 IPs now via infra-net:
```
infra-net block-cidr 198.51.100.0/24 --scope velara-vpc --reason "signed-url spike"
```
Jin Lee - oncall: Pulled agent logs — there are createSignedUrl API calls at 12:12:07 UTC from principal service/velara-urlgen; source IP 10.12.8.5 (private worker).
Inga Audit: Raw S3 access logs pulled. Found matching GETs and sign-create events. The create events originated from a long-running worker pod in the customer's private cluster (10.12.8.5). Evidence exported to /evidence/velara/incident-1801234567.tar.gz
Samir (sec): That suggests possible compromise on the customer side (a worker with creds). Still, we must rotate our signing principal to be safe and tighten RBAC on the generator API. Maria, please tell Velara to isolate that worker and rotate any creds they manage.
Maria C.: Call scheduled with Velara security at 15:30 UTC. I've told them we will rotate keys and provide the exported logs.
Jin Lee - oncall: Rotating signing principal now. Command: 
```
infra-identity rotate-key --principal service/s3sign-velara --force --note "sec-incident-1801234567"
```
logbot: Rotation completed: key id rk-9f4b rotated. Audit entry id: 1801234670.
Samir (sec): Post-incident actions (prioritized):
1) alert: signed-url-creation-rate > 20/min for any tenant -> page sec oncall
2) RBAC: disallow service principals from issuing signed URLs with expiry > 24h
3) improve audit pipeline to ensure <2m ingestion lag for private tenants
4) ensure evidence bundle retention + SLA for exports
Inga Audit: I'll take the audit-lag ticket and create INC-1245. Exported evidence uploaded and signed. Creating Jira tasks for retention and alerting.
Maria C.: Thanks team. I'll update Velara after the 15:30 call and confirm when their worker is isolated. Owners: Samir (sec) lead, Jin (infra ops) rotation & block, Inga (audit) evidence & pipeline.
Samir (sec): Also add a short postmortem template for the customer: timeline, containment, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, next steps. We should turn that into a runbook item for private tenants.
Maria C.: Will draft the postmortem and send to the customer and internal stakeholders after the call. Closing interim status here. :thumbsup:
